title: CHAPTER XX. A Good Imagination Gone Wrong
chineseTitle: 第 20 章：走火入魔的想象力

paragraphs.en: Spring returned to Green Gables with its characteristic Canadian charm, lingering through April and May in cool, sweet days. The maples in Lover’s Lane were budding red, and little ferns sprouted around the Dryad’s Bubble. In the barrens behind Mr. Silas Sloane's property, pink and white Mayflowers bloomed under brown leaves.
paragraphs.zh: 春天带着典型的加拿大风情回到了绿山墙，逗留到了四月和五月，带来了凉爽而甜蜜的日子。情人小径上的枫树开始绽放红色的新芽，而林间的露珠蕨丛中也冒出了嫩绿的小叶。在塞拉斯·斯洛恩先生地产后面的荒野中，粉白相间的五月花在褐色的叶片下悄然绽放。

paragraphs.en: Anne lamented to Marilla about those who lacked Mayflowers, believing they couldn't be missed if unknown. "I think it would be tragic not to know what Mayflowers are like," she said. "They must be the souls of flowers that died last summer."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮对玛丽拉倾诉，那些没有见过五月花的人真是可惜，认为他们如果没有见过也不会有什么不同。“我觉得根本不知道什么是五月花真是太遗憾了，”她说，“它们一定是去年夏天死去的花朵的灵魂。”

paragraphs.en: The girls and boys had a delightful day gathering them, picnicking by an old well in a mossy hollow. Charlie Sloane dared Arty Gillis to jump over it; Arty did, as no one else would dare.
paragraphs.zh: 孩子们在苔藓覆盖的洼地旁旧井边野餐，收集那些花朵，度过了愉快的一天。查理·斯洛恩敢向阿蒂·吉尔思发起挑战，让他跳过那口井；阿蒂真的跳了过去，因为没有人愿意冒险。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Phillips gave Mayflowers to Prissy Andrews, showing he had some imagination. Anne refused any offered flowers with disdain. They made wreaths and marched home singing "My Home on the Hill," creating quite a sensation along the way.
paragraphs.zh: 菲利普斯先生给了普西·安德鲁斯一些月季花，显示出他还是有些想象力的。安妮不屑地拒绝了任何送来的花朵。她们编好了花环，唱着《山上的家园》，一路高歌，引得路人纷纷侧目。

paragraphs.en: Marilla responded, "Not much wonder! Such silly doings!"
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉回应说：“难怪！这么荒唐的事！”

paragraphs.en: In June, when the orchards bloomed pink and frogs sang sweetly by Lake Shining Waters, Anne sat by her gable window, lost in thought. She had been studying but the darkness made reading impossible, so she gazed out past the Snow Queen's blossoms.
paragraphs.zh: 六月里，当果园里的花朵粉嫩绽放，湖畔传来了青蛙悦耳的歌声时，安妮坐在绿山墙的窗前，陷入了沉思。她本在温习功课，但夜色已深，读书变得不可能，于是她凝视着窗外雪皇后那绚烂的花海。

paragraphs.en: The room remained unchanged—white walls, a hard pincushion, stiff chairs—but it felt different now. It was filled with a vibrant energy, as if Anne’s dreams and waking thoughts had taken visible form, weaving a tapestry of rainbow and moonlight across the bare space.
paragraphs.zh: 房间依旧未变——白墙、硬邦邦的针垫和僵直的椅子，但如今感觉大不相同。这里弥漫着一股生机勃勃的能量，仿佛安妮的梦想与清醒时的想法化作了有形的存在，在这片空旷的空间中编织出一道道彩虹与月光的绚烂图景。

paragraphs.en: Marilla entered briskly, bringing freshly ironed school aprons for Anne. She hung them on a chair and sat down, sighing. She had suffered from a headache that day but felt weak and "tuckered out," as she said.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉利索地走进来，带来了刚熨好的校服围裙给安妮。她把围裙挂在椅子上，然后坐下叹了口气。她那天头痛不已，但感觉虚弱疲惫，正如她说的那样，“累坏了”。

paragraphs.en: Anne looked at her with sympathetic eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮用同情的目光看着她。

paragraphs.en: "I truly wish I could have your headache today, Marilla. I would endure it gladly for you."
paragraphs.zh: “玛利亚拉，我真的希望今天能替你忍受头痛。我会乐意承受的。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla said, "You did well with the work, letting me rest. Starching Matthew’s handkerchiefs wasn't necessary, and people usually take pies out of the oven to eat them. But you let this pie burn.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉说：“你把活儿干得不错，让我休息了。给马修的手帕打浆并不必要，人们通常都是出炉就把派端出来吃。不过这次你把派给烧焦了。”

paragraphs.en: You were trying not to imagine, but ended up thinking about an enchanted princess in a tower."
paragraphs.zh: 你本不想胡思乱想，结果却想到了塔中的魔法公主。

paragraphs.en: Anne replied, "I was so focused on naming our new island Victoria that I forgot the pie. I didn’t know I starched the handkerchiefs while ironing. It’s an anniversary today, Marilla.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮回答说：“我全心想着给这个新岛起名叫维多利亚，结果忘了烤馅饼的事。我不知在熨手帕时还把它们先用淀粉打湿了。今天是个纪念日，玛丽拉。”

paragraphs.en: Do you remember my first day at Green Gables last year?"
paragraphs.zh: 你还记得我去年初来绿山墙的第一天吗？

paragraphs.en: Marilla responded, "No, not really."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉回答说：“不，严格来说不是这样的。”

paragraphs.en: Anne continued, "That was a turning point in my life. You might not see it as important, but I’ve been happy here for a year despite troubles. Are you glad you kept me, Marilla?"
paragraphs.zh: 安妮继续说道：“那是一个人生的转折点。你可能不会觉得这很重要，但尽管这里有过不少波折，我还是在这里度过了快乐的一年。你还真高兴没把我送走，玛丽拉？”

paragraphs.en: Marilla said, "Not sorry at all. Sometimes I wonder how I lived before you came to Green Gables."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉说：“一点也不后悔。有时候我还真纳闷，要不是你来绿山墙，我以前是怎么过的。”

paragraphs.en: Anne added, "It’s too dark to ask Mrs. Barry about the apron pattern."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮补充说：“天太暗了，没法去问巴里太太那块围裙的图案是什么样的。”

paragraphs.en: Anne was eager to visit the property at twilight but decided to go early morning instead. Marilla, needing her help with an apron pattern, urged her to leave immediately.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮本打算在黄昏时分去参观那块地产，但最终决定清晨就出发。玛丽拉正需要她的帮助来设计围裙图案，便催促她赶紧走。

paragraphs.en: Reluctantly, Anne agreed to take a longer route around the road rather than through the Haunted Wood. When Marilla questioned why she couldn't bypass it, Anne pleaded that the wood was too scary.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮不情愿地同意绕路走，而不是穿过那片令人毛骨悚然的幽灵林。当玛丽拉问她为什么不能绕过去时，安妮央求说那片树林太可怕了。

paragraphs.en: Marilla stared in disbelief. "Haunted Wood? Are you crazy?
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉难以置信地瞪大了眼睛。“幽灵林？你是不是疯了？”

paragraphs.en: What is this nonsense?"
paragraphs.zh: “这胡说八道是什么东西？”

paragraphs.en: Anne whispered, "It's the spruce grove over the brook."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮低声道：“那是小溪那边的云杉林。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla dismissed the idea. "There’s no such thing as a haunted wood. Who told you this?"
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉否定了这个想法：“根本就没有闹鬼的树林这回事。是谁告诉你的？”

paragraphs.en: Anne admitted, "Diana and I just imagined it for fun. We started in April because it seemed so common here. A haunted wood is romantic.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮承认：“戴安娜和我只是图个乐子想象出来的。我们是从四月开始的，因为这里这样的幽灵林太常见了，倒也平添了几分浪漫。”

paragraphs.en: We thought of a white lady walking by the brook at night, and a murdered child's ghost that touches your hand."
paragraphs.zh: 我们想到了一个白裙女士在夜晚溪边漫步，还有那触碰你手的谋杀案中孩子的鬼魂。

paragraphs.en: Marilla was astonished. "Do you really believe this nonsense?"
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉惊讶不已，“你真的相信这种胡说八道？”

paragraphs.en: Anne faltered, "Not exactly. I don't believe it in daylight but after dark, Marilla, ghosts walk."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮犹豫着说：“不完全是这样。我白天下不信有鬼，但到了晚上，玛丽拉，我相信鬼魂会行走。”

paragraphs.en: Anne pleaded with Marilla, her fear genuine. She had heard stories from respectable people about haunted woods, including Charlie Sloane's grandmother and Mrs. Thomas’s father. But Marilla was firm.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮向玛丽拉恳求，语气中带着真实的恐惧。她从一些正直的人那里听说过闹鬼的树林，包括查理·斯洛恩的祖母和汤姆斯太太的父亲。但玛丽拉的态度却很坚定。

paragraphs.en: She marched Anne to the spring and ordered her to cross the bridge into the dark grove where headless spirits supposedly roamed.
paragraphs.zh: 她领着安妮来到泉水边，命令她穿过小桥进入那片据说游荡着无头幽灵的黑暗林地。

paragraphs.en: "Marilla, how can you be so cruel?" Anne cried. "What would you feel like if a white thing snatched me up?"
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉，你怎么能这么残忍？”安妮喊道，“如果你突然被一个白色的东西抓走，你会有什么感觉？”

paragraphs.en: "I'll risk it," Marilla replied coldly. "I always mean what I say. You’ll learn not to imagine ghosts in places."
paragraphs.zh: “我冒这个险。”玛丽拉冷冰冰地回答。“我一向说话算数。你会学到不要在想象中看到鬼影。”

paragraphs.en: Anne walked cautiously over the bridge and up the dark path. She never forgot that terrifying journey. Her imagination had conjured goblins in every shadow, reaching out to grab her.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮小心翼地点过木桥，沿着幽暗的小径前行。她从未忘记那次令人恐惧的旅程。她的想象力在每一个阴影中编织出了妖魔的形象，仿佛它们伸手欲抓她。

paragraphs.en: A strip of birch bark blowing from a hollow made her heart race. The sound of rubbing boughs caused beads of sweat on her forehead. Bats swooping overhead seemed like unearthly creatures.
paragraphs.zh: 一片桦树皮在空洞中飘动，让她的心跳加速。树枝摩擦的声音让她额头冒出了汗珠。飞掠而过的蝙蝠仿佛成了不祥之物。

paragraphs.en: Reaching Mr. William Bell's field, Anne ran across it as if pursued by white things. She arrived at the Barry kitchen panting and asked for an apron pattern without delay. Marilla was unsympathetic when she asked, "So nothing caught you?"
paragraphs.zh: 抵达威廉·贝尔先生的田地后，安妮仿佛被什么白色的东西追赶着一般飞奔而过。她气喘吁吁地赶到巴里家的厨房，立刻请求拿一个围裙图案。玛丽拉在问她“难道是有什么东西追上你了吗？”时，并没有表现出同情的态度。

paragraphs.en: Anne replied, trembling, "Oh, Mar—Marilla, I'll be content with commonplace places after this."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮颤抖着回答：“哦，玛——玛丽拉，经历了这次之后，我甘心去平凡的地方了。”
